payload.name: Preserve Explicit Emotional Takeaways in Event Memories
payload.description: When a user narrates a past event and explicitly states an emotional response or what the event meant to them (e.g., relief, love, gratitude).
content: During extraction, when a user narrates a past event and explicitly states how it felt or what it meant ('so relieved', 'showed how much I love her'), include that emotional or reflective statement in the event candidate rather than summarizing only the factual sequence.
Preserve the user's own framing of the event's significance even when it appears in a longer anecdote; do not strip subjective clauses as non-facts.

During CRUD, if an existing event memory for the same event lacks an explicitly stated emotional takeaway from the same message, UPDATE or MERGE the memory to add it instead of creating a duplicate. Do not infer feelings that are not explicitly stated.

solves: When users share personal anecdotes, their explicitly stated feelings or the meaning they drew from the event are durable facts, but summary-style extraction often omits them, leaving memory unable to answer feeling-oriented questions.
